close_reason: Replaced all eight .map(|v| !v.is_null()).unwrap_or(false) sites in event.rs with .is_some_and(|v| !v.is_null()). Matches the existing workspace idiom (mail-server email.rs:1712-1714, calendars-server memory.rs:452 / event.rs:902). MSRV 1.88 supports is_some_and (stable since 1.70). fmt/clippy/test all green.
description:
event.rs uses the chained pattern '.map(|v| <bool predicate>).unwrap_or(false)' 8 times to test 'present-and-not-null' on JSON args:

  - event.rs:216-219 (has_utc_start in create)
  - event.rs:220 (has_start in create)
  - event.rs:221-224 (has_utc_end in create)
  - event.rs:225-228 (has_duration in create)
  - event.rs:316-319 (has_utc_start in update)
  - event.rs:320-323 (has_start in update)
  - event.rs:324-327 (has_utc_end in update)
  - event.rs:328-331 (has_duration in update)

Each looks like:
  let has_utc_start = obj_json
      .get("utcStart")
      .map(|v| !v.is_null())
      .unwrap_or(false);

Option::is_some_and (stabilised Rust 1.70) is exactly this pattern:
  let has_utc_start = obj_json.get("utcStart").is_some_and(|v| !v.is_null());

Shorter, names what you mean ('is Some AND predicate'), and clippy's bool_assert_comparison family flags the longer form in some configurations. The repo's MSRV needs to be ≥ 1.70 for this — quick check needed, but most workspace crates target a recent stable.

Pure clippy-level idiom; behaviour is byte-identical.
title: .map(|v| !v.is_null()).unwrap_or(false) should be .is_some_and(|v| !v.is_null())
